title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Moving Certificate Proceeds Out of Savings
content:
A certificate of deposit often pays its interest, and eventually its maturity or grace-period proceeds, into a Savings & Money Market Accounts product of the same owner. This page covers an owner's request to send that certificate's money back out of the savings or money market account to one of their own Personal Checking accounts.

## What the policy governs

- **The situation.** The owner asks for the money put into the account by the certificate of deposit that paid into it most recently to be moved out of the account.
- **The result it governs.** The dollar amount that leaves: the money from that certificate that is still sitting in the account. A request aimed at the money of some other certificate falls outside this policy.
- **The handling.** The money leaves as a telephone withdrawal from the savings or money market account into a checking account of the owner's own.
- **The effect.** The withdrawal is subject, on the day it posts, to every rule that governs paying withdrawals and the per-cycle allowance. Because the owner gives the instruction personally over the telephone, it is activity initiated by the customer for dormancy purposes.

## Carrying out the transfer

The owner performs this transfer; the agent does not. The agent unlocks `transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b` for the owner with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`, and the customer themselves then submits it through `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**What the tool does.** One submission posts one withdrawal on the savings or money market account through the telephone banking channel, with a fresh posting trace number, and names the receiving checking account as the other side of the movement. The balance falls by the amount straight away. The posted date is the business day of posting: the day itself when it is Monday to Friday and not a Federal Reserve holiday, otherwise the next such day. The withdrawal then appears in the account's activity under the reference the tool returns.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `savings_account_id` | reference number of the savings or money market account the money leaves, as the savings account lookup returns it | identifier |
| `destination_checking_account_id` | reference number of the owner's own checking account that receives the money, as the checking account lookup returns it | identifier |
| `amount` | the sum moved | US dollars, positive, two decimal places |
| `statement_cycle` | the statement cycle in which the withdrawal posts | `YYYY-MM`, the month in which the cycle containing the posted date closes |

## What comes back

A text rendering of a dictionary with `savings_txn_id` (reference of the posted withdrawal), `posted_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `amount` (dollars, two decimals), `channel` (always `telephone_banking`), `trace_number` (15 digits) and `new_balance` (the account balance after the withdrawal, two decimals). The presence of a `savings_txn_id` confirms that the withdrawal posted.

## Points of judgement

**Is this transfer something the agent submits on the owner's behalf?** No. It is the owner's own instruction, handed over for the owner to run.

**Does moving certificate money set aside the usual withdrawal rules?** No. It is an ordinary telephone withdrawal as far as payment, the allowance and any excess charge are concerned, judged on the day it posts.
